validity.researcher_notes: wiki_citations.json is empty for this row (gem.wiki 403'd the whole scrape this run, per scope notes) and my own WebFetch of https://www.gem.wiki/Krapa-Manjiwala_Gas_Pipeline also returned HTTP 403 - so there is nothing the sheet itself cites to re-verify; this had to be ground-up open-web research, and it came back essentially empty. A DuckDuckGo HTML search for "Krapa" "Manjiwala" gas pipeline returned exactly ONE result on the whole page: the GEM wiki page itself (www.gem.wiki/Krapa-Manjiwala_Gas_Pipeline) - no other site, news article, SNGPL document, or map mentions this pipeline by name anywhere on the open web that I could reach. Bing and Google searches for the same and related terms (adding SNGPL, Karak, Pezu, cement) returned degraded/irrelevant boilerplate (US gas-station locators, unrelated ads) with zero on-topic hits - not usable as either confirming or disconfirming evidence, just noise. This session's WebSearch tool budget was exhausted (200/200 used) partway through, and the Wayback Machine is unfetchable from this environment, so I could not pull an archived pre-Cloudflare copy of the gem.wiki page to see what it used to cite either. GAZETTEER CHECK: neither endpoint place-name resolves in Pakistan on OpenStreetMap Nominatim. "Krapa" matches villages/islands in Finland, Latvia, Ghana, Guyana, India (Andhra Pradesh) and North Macedonia - none in Pakistan. "Manjiwala" matches only a village in Pachpadra Tehsil, Rajasthan, INDIA - not Pakistan. "Kala Manjiwala" (GEM's own EndLocation string) returns zero results. Wikipedia's Karak_District article explicitly names the district's gas-producing localities - Makori, Noshpa Banda, Gurguri, Lachi circle - and does NOT mention Krapa or Manjiwala anywhere; Lakki_Marwat_District and Pezu (the town P4178 supposedly continues to) likewise make no mention of a gas pipeline, Manjiwala, or Krapa. CAVEAT ON THE NEGATIVE GAZETTEER SIGNAL: I sanity-checked whether OSM simply has poor coverage of rural KP by searching for 'Gurguri' (the Wikipedia-confirmed real gas locality in Karak, and itself a roster row: P4182 Gurguri-Kohat) - it ALSO returns zero OSM results, so the absence of Krapa/Manjiwala from OSM is not, by itself, conclusive of non-existence; it may just reflect generally thin rural-KP toponym coverage. I am therefore NOT treating the OSM/Wikipedia gaps as proof the pipeline is fake, only as failing to provide the independent confirmation the sweep protocol requires - combined with total absence from open-web search (where a real 84 km SNGPT transmission trunk would ordinarily leave at least a passing trace in news, OGRA filings, or engineering literature), this clears the bar for an existence flag per the standing rule ('the ONLY traces are GEM-derived ... you cannot find independent confirmation -> concern/existence'). PLAUSIBILITY IN FAVOR (why I am not calling this a confident hallucination): the row sits inside a coherent local corridor in the roster - P4176 Kohat-Nowshera, P4177 Krapa-Manjiwala, P4178 Manjiwala-Pezu, P4182 Gurguri-Kohat all sit in the same Karak/Kohat/KP gas-producing belt Wikipedia confirms is real, and P4177/P4178 chain end-to-end (Krapa -> Manjiwala -> Pezu) the same way GEM chains other long trunks into multiple PIDs elsewhere in this roster (e.g. Sui-Multan Gas Pipeline + Loopline I/II/III). Owner = Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Ltd (SNGPL) 100% is also geographically consistent - SNGPL, not SSGC, is the utility that franchises Punjab/KP/Balochistan-north, so KP ownership by SNGPL is not itself a red flag. But internal consistency and plausibility are not independent corroboration, and I found literally none. CLASSIFICATION/ATTRIBUTION/SPEC: cannot be meaningfully assessed until existence is settled - I am not separately flagging PipelineType=transmission or Owner=SNGPL as wrong, since both are at least consistent with the surrounding corridor, but I am also not confirming them. DUPLICATE check against the 63-row roster: no other row plausibly restates this same physical segment under a different name - P4178 (Manjiwala-Pezu) is the adjacent downstream leg of the same apparent corridor, not a duplicate of P4177 itself.

summary: P4177 (Krapa-Manjiwala Gas Pipeline) flagged existence/concern: the sheet cites nothing (gem.wiki 403'd), open-web search turns up only GEM's own wiki page for this pipeline name, and neither endpoint place-name (Krapa; Kala Manjiwala) resolves anywhere in Pakistan on OSM or Wikipedia - though a same-corridor sanity check (Gurguri) shows OSM coverage of this area is generally thin, so the gap is suggestive, not conclusive; UNRESOLVED pending a primary SNGPL/OGRA network-map check with fuller source access.
